cells.tense: You are standing in what you chose, and the holding is steady right now.
cells.act: mark the good thing together, the day it happens
cells.ask: When the next hard-won thing holds, tell the ones who helped you the same day it holds. Not later. Not once it's certain. The same day.
cells.core:
Where something you've been steadying is under pressure, you can keep your direction and stay open to the ones close by. The determination you gathered doesn't harden into a wall. You hold the line and you stay reachable, and the people who helped you get there can still find you.

When the next hard-won thing holds, mark it with them the day it happens instead of waiting until it's certain. Share the good news while it's still warm and bring them close before the dust settles. Some will want to weigh in on a decision that's already made, and that's the cost of the door staying open. You get to find out who's with you.
cells.sheetLine: You hold your ground and still let people near it.
cells.verb: holding a chosen direction against what pushes on it
cells.place: the clearing where what's finished is being let go

cells.tense: You are bracing for a fight that hasn't arrived, defending ground not yet threatened.
cells.act: sit still until the calibration settles
cells.ask: Sit with the problem without solving it. No list, no call, no adjusting. Let the hour pass; when your mind quiets, go back to it.
cells.core:
Where you've chosen a direction, everything ahead gets treated as already under attack. The defense runs in advance of the threat, so the mind keeps rehearsing what might come. You gather your forces around a fight that hasn't started, and the pressure is real, and none of it is here yet.

Sit with the problem without touching it. Let the mind find its own level instead of working the angles. You'll want to adjust something; don't. What you're protecting doesn't lose anything by resting, and you may find out which part of the pressure was yours to carry and which part you invented. The hour isn't wasted. It's the ground you actually need.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed, holding a direction you no longer walk.
cells.act: keep what the change produced from drifting
cells.ask: Find one thing the ending already changed and keep it where it sits. Same spot, same order. Leave it a month without deciding what it means.
cells.core:
Something in you is still planted at the threshold. You keep the stance of holding a direction, but the thing you were holding to has already gone, and your feet haven't moved. The determination is real. It's just aimed at ground that isn't there anymore.

Instead of pushing yourself into the new room, steady one thing the ending already made. Put it somewhere fixed and keep it there. You'll feel the pull to declare what it's for, or to hurry back to defending what's finished; let that pass. What you keep holding gets to hold you too. Solid ground returns through form before it returns to your will.
cells.sheetLine: Your stance is set for a door you've already walked through.

cells.tense: You are holding things steady and calling it circumstance, not your own hand.
cells.act: form the new structure with your hands
cells.ask: Take one thing the clearing showed you and make it with your hands. Something plain, on the cleared ground. When it's finished, write your name on it.
cells.core:
Something finished, and what's standing now got steadied by choices you don't count as choices. You gather the momentum and direct it, and if someone asked you'd say things simply worked out. Meanwhile the ground is clear because you cleared it, and the direction is held because you keep holding it. The work is yours. It's been filed under luck.

Build one thing from what the clearing showed you. Make it with your hands, however plain, and keep it where you can point to it. Then claim it as yours. You'll want to say the timing was good or the conditions lined up; say the other sentence. What you claimed, you can work with. What you left unattributed, you keep having to re-earn.
cells.sheetLine: The ground is clear because you cleared it, and that goes unsaid.
